grid.max_width: 1076px (2-col dark feature grid: 538px + 538px; page container unconstrained, footer padded 24px)

taste.name: Product UI as the hero image
taste.trigger: Selling clinical software to clinic owners who cannot picture a CRM from adjectives
taste.decision: Chose real, dense product screenshots (1144x677, 1.69:1, 907-1008px rendered) tucked under a centered headline over illustration, stock clinic photography or abstract hero art
taste.reason: A practice owner buying software judges it by whether the calendar and client card look usable on their own front desk, so the screen itself is the proof
evidence: hero tab pills (Calendar, Online Booking, EMR, Workflows, Payments, Marketing) switch the screenshot
viewport 1 already clips a screenshot at y=760 of 900

taste.name: One loud CTA, everything else gray
taste.trigger: Two buttons side by side in the nav and hero, both pointing at a sales conversation
taste.decision: Chose a single saturated blue gradient button (#0073FF to #0DA2FF, 1px #0088FF border, inset #D2EAFF highlight) next to a flat #F3F4F6 secondary, over two equally colored buttons or an outline pair
taste.reason: The buyer is meant to take exactly one action, book a demo, while the tour stays available without competing for the eye
evidence: all body text #1E1B18 / #4A5565, blue appears only on CTAs, the 4,000+ figure and the logo

taste.name: Tight, negative-tracked Satoshi headlines
taste.trigger: A claim-led headline ('The only software your practice will ever need') that has to hold its own at 64px on a 1440px canvas
taste.decision: Chose one geometric sans (Satoshi, 1458 of 1501 text nodes) with letter-spacing of about -3.75% on display sizes and 1.2x line height over a serif/sans display-body pairing
taste.reason: Tight tracking makes a two-line claim read as one block, and a single family keeps the page from looking like three vendors assembled it
evidence: DM Mono 33 nodes and Inter 10 nodes, tags only

taste.name: White page, one dark island (restraint)
taste.trigger: A page with a heavy AI section (Scribe, safety checks, letters) that needs to feel different from the booking and billing sections without redecorating the whole site
taste.decision: Chose a white #FFFFFF canvas with no section borders or card shadows on light areas, and a single #0B0B14 block with 100px radius bottom corners and 24px-radius cards, over alternating tinted bands or a fully dark theme
taste.reason: The AI features get a distinct space the eye notices by contrast alone, while everything operational stays in the neutral reading mode a clinic manager already trusts
evidence: dark cards rgba(255,255,255,0.01) with 1px #202023 border, 24px radius, 2-col 538px + 538px, 24px gap
light sections separated by 100px gaps, no rules
